text:
hema: Heads up - nightly evals show a spike in failures for the longform-completion prompt set. Failure rate +4.2% vs baseline.

maria-evals-bot: nightly-run: longform-completion suite: failures 12/300 -> 24/300 (delta +4.0% absolute). Regression started 2026-03-19 23:00 UTC. Related jobs: quant-q4_8-tryout, v2-runtime.

hema: Noticed most bad gens are repetitive truncations or hallucinated lists. Quick check: did anyone change sampling defaults in the runtime? temp/top_p/top_k?

raj: I didn't touch defaults. But we rolled kernel selection tweaks for quantized models yesterday evening (PR #842). Could affect RNG paths.

liam: I see a correlation with batch-size increase in production for that route — we enabled larger continuous batching (batch_size cap 8 -> 16) in the same deploy window. Could be RNG reuse across examples.

alice-serve: Runtime sampling code uses a per-worker RNG seeded at startup. When we vectorize sampling across the batch we call .randint() per token from the same rng state. If the seeding is deterministic across restarts this is OK, but kernel changes might have changed how many RNG calls happen before sampling (leading to effective seed drift).

hema: That matches. Maria, can you pull the failing example ids? I'll try reproducing locally with the exact model/quant and the nightly config.

maria-evals-bot: Attached sample ids: [lfc-0041, lfc-0099, lfc-0210, lfc-0277]. Job metadata: model=redwood-open-7b-q4_8, sampler=stochastic, temp=0.8, top_p=0.9, top_k=50, batch=16, seed_mode=random-per-request.

raj: Two quick experiments to run: 1) force per-request seeding using OS RNG every request (instead of per-worker seeded RNG). 2) disable vectorized sampling (fallback to per-example loop) and compare failure rate.

liam: I'll repro locally. Quick script to replicate seeding: ```python
# pseudo
import torch, random, os
seed = int.from_bytes(os.urandom(8), 'little')
random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(seed)
# run generation with temp=0.8, top_p=0.9, top_k=50
```

alice-serve: Also check cuRAND vs philox differences when using CUDA-level kernels + quantized path. Some kernels use philox to advance RNG counters per-token which interacts badly with batching changes.

hema: Good point. If kernel reordering changed the number of RNG advances before sampling, we'd see distributional shifts even with same high-level config. We should test deterministic seeds with instrumented RNG counters.

raj: Proposed triage plan: (a) reproduce with same model+quant+batch locally, (b) run controlled runs toggling batch size 1/8/16 and toggling vectorized sampling, (c) run 1000 seeds with baseline runtime vs post-PR runtime and compute KL/coverage on ngram/hallucination metrics.

liam: I'll take (a)/(b). Timebox 4h. If I can reproduce, I'll attach diffs and failing gens.

alice-serve: I'll add a quick runtime toggle to disable continuous batching for that route as a temporary mitigation (config flag). If that reduces failures we can roll-back batching until kernel fixes land.

ci-bot: deploy-trigger: created rollback-config branch -> disable-continuous-batching-longform. Tests queued.

hema: Thanks. If anyone finds a minimal repro script that deterministically flips outputs based on seed/state, drop it here. Also capture RNG call counts before sampling to show drift.

maria-evals-bot: Noted — will re-run nightly with the disable-batching flag and report delta tomorrow morning.

hema: Perfect. Assign follow-ups: liam = repro + data, alice-serve = temporary config + monitor, raj = kernel PR bisect if repro shows kernel-level cause. Ping me for priority escalation. :thumbsup:

liam: On it.

raj: Will start bisecting if liam reproduces.

alice-serve: Putting a small dashboard alert to watch longform route error rate and sample entropy shift.

hema: Great, thanks team. Keep thread small updates only.
